question: The perimeter of a square is 160 m. Find its area (in m²).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Side of the square = Perimeter ÷ 4

Side = 160 ÷ 4 = 40 m

Area = Side × Side = 40 × 40 = 1600 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1600 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Perimeter of the square = 160 m

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a (where a is the side length)

Area of a square = a²

 
 a = 40 m
 a = 40 m
 Area = 1600 sq. m
 Perimeter = 160 m
 
• 
 
•

 a

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4 × a = 160

⇒ a = 160 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 40 m

⇒ Area = a × a

⇒ Area = 40 × 40

⇒ Area = 1600 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 1600 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Diagonal of a Square

The diagonal (d) of a square with side 'a' is given by d = a√2.

Area of a Square (using Diagonal)

The area can also be directly calculated from its diagonal as A = d² ÷ 2.

Perimeter of a Rectangle

The perimeter of a rectangle is P = 2 × (l + b), where l is the length and b is the breadth.
